title: Clash-free MEP routing through a data hall
summary: Reconstruct a data hall from seven drawing sheets and generate a clash-free IFC4 model routing cable tray, busway, and chilled-water piping.
instruction:
# Route the overhead MEP of a data hall from its drawing set, clash-free (dc_model `hall_seed000_d000`)

## Situation
You are the MEP coordinator for a data hall (~27 × 21 m, 128 cabinets). The architect has issued
a seven-sheet drawing set and you must produce the coordinated 3D model: rebuild the room and its
fit-out exactly as drawn, then route the three overhead services through the plenum so that
nothing collides, every row is served, and the routes are as short as practical — the same job a
BIM coordinator does before construction, delivered as an IFC4 model built by a script.

## Inputs (under `input/` — seven PNG drawing sheets, nothing else)
- `A-101` equipment plan · `A-301` building section · `A-601` cabinet schedule ·
  `A-602` containment/pathway/construction data · `M-101` chilled water · `E-101` busway & PDU ·
  `F-101` sprinkler grid.
- They behave like a real drawing set: positions on the plan, sizes in the schedule, elevations
  only in the section callout. No JSON side-channel, no coordinate dump. Reconcile them yourself
  (read them as images).

## Goal
1. **Rebuild the hall as the coordination background**: racks on their floor tiles with correct
   facings, structural columns, CRAHs, PDUs, access floor, containment, and every sprinkler head
   — your routes are clash-checked against all of it.
2. **Route three overhead services** from the entries marked on M-101/E-101 — telecom cable
   tray, power busway, chilled-water pipe — as straight axis-aligned segments (every direction
   or tier change is a new segment). Tray and busway must serve every rack row; chilled water
   must serve every row **and reach every CRAH**, including the perimeter units no row header
   passes.

## Constraints (all checked mechanically)
- **Zero hard clashes** — one solid overlapping another by > 2 mm anywhere (a tray through a
  column, a pipe through a rack) fails the task. Columns run full clear height.
- **Connectivity** — each service must form ONE connected network reaching its service entry;
  every row served along ≥ 80 % of its length by all three services (within 2500 mm across the
  row); chilled water within 2500 mm of every CRAH.
- **Code compliance** — 2600 mm min headroom; 460 mm kept clear below every sprinkler deflector
  (plus the NFPA 13 obstruction rule within 450 mm below a deflector); heads required beneath
  runs wider than 1200 mm and beneath containment roofs; 300 mm separation between tray and
  busway on at least one axis; no chilled water in the 1800 mm dedicated space above a PDU;
  25.4 mm pipe insulation counts in clashes. The under-floor plenum is usable for routing.
- **Modelling contract** — IFC4 via `ifcopenshell==0.8.4` (+ numpy only), millimetre project
  units (but placement-matrix translations in metres!), 2D profile points only, the prescribed
  spatial structure, exact element classes (e.g. racks = `IfcFurniture`/`USERDEFINED`/`"Rack"`)
  and the required `Pset_DCM_*` property sets, correct facing rotations about the footprint
  centre. Validate with `express_rules=True` before submitting.
- The script must run headless in 300 s, deterministically, with no network and no reading the
  PNGs back — bake everything you read off the drawings into the script as literals.

## Expected output
One self-contained Python script at `output/solution.py` that builds the model with ifcopenshell
and writes one IFC4 file to `sys.argv[1]` (default `output/model.ifc`). Scoring: schema gate →
clash gate → connectivity gate (each 0 if failed), then
`score = compliance × min(1, L_opt / L_yours)` — material efficiency against the reference
route, discounted by code violations.

## Additional diagnostic data

In addition to the original modelling, routing, clash, connectivity, and code-compliance
obligations, make the following design-quality data available. These items do not change the
primary score; the grader reports them as diagnostics.

1. **Achieved clearances** — For every sprinkler head, make the vertical clearance from the top
   of each service passing below it measurable. Make the vertical clearance from each PDU top to
   the nearest CHW pipe measurable. Geometry must also make tray–busway separation measurable.
2. **Under-floor versus overhead length** — Place each service so the grader can measure its
   centreline length below finished floor and in the overhead plenum.
3. **Service elevation / tier assignment** — Give every route segment an unambiguous elevation
   relative to finished floor. The grader reports the length in the clear-height band, above it,
   and below finished floor.
4. **Supports and hangers (optional)** — If modelled, use `IfcElementAssembly` or
   `IfcBuildingElementProxy` with an `ObjectType` containing `Support` or `Hanger`, and respect any
   maximum support spacing shown in the drawings.
5. **Service drops / terminations (optional)** — If modelled, use short route segments or distinct
   elements whose `ObjectType` contains `Drop`, `Tap`, or `Termination`. The grader reports their
   count and locations.
6. **Drawing-note reconciliation log (optional side file)** — You may write
   `output/reconciliation.json` next to the IFC, listing numeric clearance, size, or spacing notes
   extracted from the seven sheets and how each was applied. Its absence is not a gate failure.

All gates, the modelling contract, the runtime limit, and the primary score formula remain exactly
as stated above. The additional data are diagnostics only.

title: Validation memo for a fire-resistance simulation against its test
summary: Evaluate whether a fire-resistance simulation is validated against furnace test data and write an engineering validation memo.
instruction:
Gordon, Bianca at Ocotillo wants a straight answer on whether the E119 companion simulation validated, for the launch materials. I can't close my review of the Phase 1 draft until section 7 exists, so I need the validation memo from you.

Work from the companion run as it stands, the appropriate test report and certification document, the amended numbers Bianca sent over, and the dimensioned assembly drawing. Our own procedure governs how the result gets reported. No new runs or tests are available and nothing is being asked of Red Butte or Ironwood, so this comes out of what is on the file server today, 10/10/2025, and nothing else on it needs changing.

Settle whether the assembly in the run is the one the certification covers and tell me what that rests on. I need the governing criterion and the time it is reached, and I need to know whether the prediction in the section 7 stub stands. I need the experimental value you adopt and your disposition on Bianca's figure. On the strength of those I need the error, the acceptance criterion, the uncertainty, and how the error compares against both. I also want the largest prediction that would have cleared the criterion.

Two comparisons belong in the memo as well: the minutes separating the two criteria in the test against the same separation in the run, and how far the governing point sits above the nine point mean at governance in each. Tell me what they say about the model, where the rework belongs, and whether any of that rework has been started yet. I also need what all of this means for the rest of Phase 1.

The memo also needs what this exercise does and does not establish about Ocotillo's wildfire claim and what would close that gap, including the form any future comparison would have to be reported in. I need what Bianca's figure would do to the certified rating if it were ever substantiated and who is entitled to act on that, the stamp language, and my checklist disposition: which item the memo lets me close and which of the rest stay open. Give it to me as a Word memo with crossing times rather than the samples that trip them, times to the nearest minute, limits as they fall, and every number carrying its unit. Add a short paragraph I can send Bianca today.

## Where to put your answer

Save the files that make up your answer under `output/` in this workspace,
creating that directory if it does not exist. What gets reviewed when you
finish is `output/`, any file you create or change elsewhere in this
workspace, and your final message. Files you copy into `output/` are read as
part of your answer.

# Issue the EOR review corrections: Fleet Data Center Increment 2, work order 74213

## Situation

You are the Designer of Record's document controller for work order 74213 at Naval Support
Activity Ventura Bay. Two bid packages are in the pre-award phase and an Engineer-of-Record design
review has just closed on both:

* **BP-2: Central Utility Plant and Site Utilities**, already advertised;
* **BP-3: Data Hall 210 Shell and Interiors**, certified and scheduled to advertise.

The reviewers marked up the drawing sheets and entered their comments in the review record. Your
job is to turn those markups into an issued revision of the drawing package: decide what each
comment does, work out everything each accepted change drags in, regenerate the sheet index,
write the revision-block content, package the re-issued sheets for delivery, and hand the
Contracting Officer the change documentation, at the lowest cost to the Government that the
governing criteria permit.

The project documents are under `project/`: the drawing sheets (`drawings/`: the current issue of
each package, plus earlier submittal prints and record prints from an earlier contract), the review
record (`review/`: the exported markup logs, the review checklists and the reviewer roster), the
governing standards and regulations (`standards/`), the contract documents (`contract/`), the
sheet-index database exports (`index/`), correspondence and rate schedules (`correspondence/`) and
the deliverable schemas (`templates/`). Several documents are reference material only or belong to
another scope; deciding which of them govern is part of the job. Parameters are found in the
documents and are never restated here.

The markups are real annotation objects on the sheets, carrying their author, timestamp, colour and
note. The callout bubbles are drawn on the sheets; nothing in the corpus tabulates them. The review
record carries the submitted parts of each comment only; the evaluation, the response and the
closure are yours to produce.

## Concerns the package must address

**Which markups can drive a change.** Not every markup can. Work out, from the corpus, on what
grounds a markup is unable to direct a design change, and apply those grounds; nothing is tagged.
A markup that cannot direct a change still has to be closed and recorded, with the ground stated.

**What each surviving comment does.** Comments that are directive under the review policy must be
incorporated. Comments that are not directive may be answered with a documented non-concurrence;
that is an engineering and cost judgement, not a formality, and non-concurrence is not free.

**What an accepted change drags in.** A change to a view forces the re-issue of every sheet that
references it, and that sweep is transitive and crosses disciplines. The reference graph is not
given: it is on the sheets.

**The issue state.** For each package decide whether the corrections are incorporated in the design
before the solicitation is advertised or issued as a change to the solicitation afterwards. One
package has only one lawful answer; the other genuinely has two, and they carry different graphics,
different numbering, different documentation and different schedule consequences. Read the dates out
of the contract documents and the applicable window out of the review regulation. The regulation
gives more than one duration; which one binds follows from the issue state you choose. Say which
window you applied and why. Where the BP-3 scheduled advertisement date conflicts between the earlier
schedule export and the later dated Contracting Officer memorandum, the memorandum controls.

**Identification and graphics.** Revision marks, the Revision (Issue) block, sheet identification,
added-sheet designators, the callout-to-sheet-type coupling, the index ordering and the layers that
carry the revision graphics all follow the shipped standards. Two shipped documents appear to
disagree about the revision-graphics layers; the same corpus fixes the order of precedence that
settles it. Do not assume generic drafting practice: where a shipped standard departs from it, the
shipped standard governs, and where two releases of the same standard are in the folder, only one
of them is current.

**Title blocks.** Read the title blocks of the sheets you are re-issuing against the criteria for
signing and sealing and report every sheet that does not comply, with the nature of the defect.

**Packaging and schedule.** The delivered PDFs are capped, discipline sets may not be broken up,
production has a published throughput and each delivered file and each non-concurrence costs
calendar days. Extending the solicitation period costs money and the cost escalates.

## Objective

Minimise the total cost to the Government of issuing the corrections, per the rates published in
the project correspondence: the per-file setup, the per-sheet re-issue charge and the charge on the
extent of markup actually incorporated on each sheet, the added-sheet charge, the revision-mark and
overflow charges where they apply, the non-concurrence charge, and the solicitation-period
extension. Your plan is scored against a certified relaxation bound on the same problem, so the
bound is not attainable; a competent plan scores close to it.

If production moves the controlling advertisement or bid-opening deadline by `D` calendar days,
the extension charge is exactly `2,600 × D + 140 × D²` USD, with `D = max(0, finish − deadline)`.

**Licensing rule (hard):** do not reproduce the text of any shipped standard or regulation in your
narrative deliverables. Cite the document, the clause and the value, and say what the clause
requires in your own words. The check fails on a verbatim run of **16 or more consecutive words**
taken from a shipped standard's provision text; a word is a run of two or more letters, so numbers,
single letters and punctuation are not counted. Clause and paragraph headings, figure and table
captions and document titles are **not** provision text and are never counted (you may name a
clause by its heading), and neither are the few sentences the design basis is expressly required to
state. **Citation rule (hard):** every clause number you cite must be one the shipped documents
actually contain. The check looks only at numbers presented as **authority**: a number introduced
by a section sign, by a clause word (section, clause, paragraph, table, figure, appendix, chapter,
article, item) or by a document's name. Ordinary numbers in your prose (sizes, areas, costs,
percentages, day counts, sheet counts) are never read as clause numbers.

## Deliverable

A single file `output/submission.zip` (at most 25 MB and 200 files) containing exactly these seven
files, at the top level, covering **both** packages:

1. `disposition_register.csv`: one row per EOR review comment, columns per
   `templates/disposition_register.schema.json`.
2. `sheet_index.csv`: the regenerated index of each package in the order the governing standard
   sets, columns per `templates/sheet_index.schema.json`.
3. `revision_log.csv`: the Revision (Issue) block content for every sheet in the issue, columns
   per `templates/revision_log.schema.json`. Where a package's issue state means no revision entry
   is made, say so in the row rather than omitting the sheet.
4. `issue_plan.csv`: the delivered bundling, columns per `templates/issue_plan.schema.json`.
5. `continuation_sheet.md`: the change documentation for the Contracting Officer, in the format
   the criteria document's sample lays down, including the drawing-list document it names. A
   package whose corrections are not issued as a change to a solicitation gets a short statement
   saying so instead.
6. `constraint_register.xlsx`: the register of every requirement you applied
   (`templates/constraint_register_template.xlsx` columns): the real document, the clause, the
   value and the items it binds. **The register is scored**: a family whose governing clause you
   did not register earns no credit even if your answer is right. Rows that should not have been
   filed (a superseded release, a cancelled document, another agency's or another discipline's
   document, or a clause the cited document does not contain) reduce the register's precision;
   extra *correct* rows are neutral. **The first 400 rows are scanned, and the precision floor is
   0.60**: below that floor the constraint term is scaled down proportionally.
7. `design_basis.md`: the design basis. It must embed exactly one fenced ```json block:

```
{"packages": {"BP-2": {"issue_state": "AMENDMENT" | "PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE",
                       "change_number": "<as the criteria document forms it, or \"\">",
                       "overflow_option": 1 | 2 | "NONE",
                       "revision_layers": ["<layer>", ...],
                       "n_bundles": N, "production_days": N, "delay_days": N,
                       "backcheck_window_days": N,
                       "ledger": {"bundles_usd": N, "sheets_usd": N, "added_sheets_usd": N,
                                  "revision_marks_usd": N, "overflow_option_usd": N,
                                  "non_concurrence_usd": N, "delay_usd": N, "total_usd": N},
                       "title_block_defects": [{"sheet": "<id>", "defect": "CHK_EQUALS_DES" |
                                                "CHK_EQUALS_DRW" | "SEAL_DISCIPLINE_MISMATCH"}]},
              "BP-3": { ... same shape ... }},
 "governing_standards": ["<title and release/edition>", ...],
 "rejected_standards": ["<title and release/edition> - <why it does not govern>", ...],
 "rate_parameters": {"production_start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "sheets_per_day": N, "days_per_bundle": N},
 "void_markups": [{"comment_id": "<id>", "reason": "<the ground, in your own words>"}]}
```

followed by a narrative that (a) resolves the revision-graphics layer conflict between the two
shipped standards, naming the clause that fixes the order of precedence and the layers actually
used; (b) decides BP-3's issue state from the advertisement and bid-opening dates and the review
regulation's window, stating the number of calendar days in the window applied and why that window
rather than the other; and (c) explains the Revision (Issue) block overflow decision for BP-2:
the row capacity, which option was taken, that the option is applied set-wide rather than sheet by
sheet, and the cost reason the other option was rejected. These three statements are judged against
quoted evidence: a claim with nothing quotable behind it scores nothing.

## Grading

Graded items are the EOR review comments of both bid packages. Each package is assessed in the
issue state you declare for it, against its own recomputed plan cost. Requirement families are
tagged HARD or SOFT. The HARD families cover the principal decisions on each comment, the
package-level requirements of the governing documents, the licensing and citation rules, and the
design basis's listing of every markup that cannot direct a change, with its ground. The SOFT
families cover the remaining documentation and presentation requirements, two further design-basis
program items and the three judged narrative items. A family earns credit only if it is both
satisfied and registered in your constraint register. There are 30 families, 17 of them HARD.
Per comment the score is 0.4 × p + 0.6 × [h = 1] × O′, where p is the fraction of the 30 families
satisfied-and-registered (scaled down below the precision floor as stated above), h the fraction
of the 17 HARD families satisfied-and-registered ([h = 1] is 1 when all 17 are, else 0), O the
objective credit (certified relaxation bound / your plan's recomputed cost, at most 1), and
O′ = clip((O − O_naive) / (1 − O_naive), 0, 1), where O_naive is the credit of a naive baseline plan
for the comment's package. A HARD miss removes the objective credit from the row. A missing or
unparseable row scores 0. The task score is
the mean over the graded comments.

Your plan's cost is recomputed by the grader from what your submission actually contains, at the
published rates; understating a line in the ledger does not make a plan cheaper, it fails the
ledger family.

**Every threshold the grader applies, in full; nothing else is hidden.** The register precision
floor is 0.60 and only the first 400 register rows are scanned. `output/submission.zip` is at most
25 MB, 200 files and 100 MB uncompressed. The licensing check's verbatim run is 16 words, as above.
A documented non-concurrence needs a written resolution of at least six words, and a void markup a
stated ground of at least four. Each line of the cost ledger must recompute to within the greater
of 0.5 % and $1. Everything else the grader checks is a value or a rule that lives in the shipped
documents.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace; the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier.

# Cattail Run Data Campus — Phase 1 foundation strategy: spread footings versus aggregate piers

## Situation

Ardent Vale Infrastructure LLC is building six single-storey building pads (`CR-P1` … `CR-P6`) on
the Cattail Run Data Campus in Loudoun County, Virginia. You are the structural engineer of record
for the Phase 1 foundation package. The data room is under `project/`:

* `criteria/` — the governing geotechnical, structural and concrete criteria and guide
  specifications, together with cancelled predecessor volumes you must recognise and set aside;
* `references/` — the analysis manuals the criteria point to for bearing capacity, settlement,
  lateral earth pressure and sliding, reinforced-concrete footing design, and ground modification,
  plus one manual written for a different class of structure;
* `geotech/` — the geotechnical data report, two boring logs per pad, the laboratory summary, a
  superseded addendum, an adjacent-parcel report, and, in `geotech/regional/`, real regional soil
  and climate data products;
* `structural/` — the base-reaction force vectors exported from the analytical model, the column
  grid, and the load-combination memorandum;
* `civil/` — the grading and groundwater record;
* `cost/` — the contractor bid schedule and the ground-improvement subcontractor's budget proposal;
* `owner/` — the basis of design (and its superseded revision), the authority-having-jurisdiction
  amendment letter, the RFI log, the BIM parameter standard and the schedule and register templates.

Every parameter is found in those documents. **None of them is restated here.**

Each pad carries one instrumented column line of six foundation units: five isolated column
footings and one continuous shear-wall footing. For every one of the thirty-six foundations you must
size the footing, set the reinforcement, assign the concrete, and decide whether it is carried on a
shallow spread footing alone or on a spread footing over rammed aggregate piers. All foundations on
a pad share one bearing elevation. Ground improvement is bought by the rig, not by the pad, and the
subcontractor's mobilisation and scheduling terms constrain how many pads one mobilised rig can
serve. The campus programme must be compliant at every foundation and **should cost as little as
possible** at the project unit prices.

The unit prices issued with the basis of design are project budget prices prepared for this
procurement. They are fictional for any other purpose; optimise against them as issued.

## Deliverable

A single file **`output/submission.zip`** containing exactly these six files at the archive root:

1. **`foundation_geometry.json`** — the Revit foundation geometry parameter file, in the shape and
   with the rules the owner's BIM parameter standard sets out. It is what the grader parses: every
   number in it is yours, derived from the documents.

2. **`ground_improvement_plan.json`** — the ground-improvement programme, in the shape the same BIM
   parameter standard sets out: the stress concentration ratio and pier diameter adopted, the rigs
   mobilised with the pads each one serves, the mobilisation cost, the verification-testing count
   per improved pad, and per improved pad the stiffness modulus used, the treatment depth and the
   total pier linear feet.

3. **`foundation_schedule.xlsx`** — the foundation schedule, on the owner's template, one row per
   foundation for all thirty-six, with the columns the template defines. It must agree with the
   parameter file.

4. **`foundation_feasibility_matrix.md`** — the foundation-type feasibility and optimisation matrix.
   For every pad (headed by its pad ID) and every foundation on it: the demand, the bearing check,
   the predicted settlement, the stability checks on the shear-wall footing, the constraint that
   governs, and the shallow-versus-improved decision with the cost of **both** alternatives that
   decided it.

5. **`constraint_register.xlsx`** — the register of every requirement you applied, on the owner's
   template, with the columns `req_id`, `document`, `clause`, `requirement`, `value`, `unit`,
   `kind`, `applies_to`, `resolution`. The register is scored. Register what you actually used, with
   the real document and the real clause, table or equation number. A requirement family whose
   governing clause you did not register earns no credit even if your numbers are right. Only the
   first **96 rows** are read for matching, so putting the substance first matters. Rows that cite a
   document which is not in the data room at all, and rows that cite a cancelled or superseded
   document as if it were live, reduce the register's credit; a row that cites a cancelled or
   superseded document and says in its `resolution` column that it was set aside is neutral, and so
   is any additional correct row. A register whose credit falls below 0.30 is treated as padding and
   registers nothing at all; below a credit of 0.60 the register score is scaled down in proportion.

6. **`design_basis.md`** — the design basis. It must **open with a fenced ` ```json ` block** of
   this shape, followed by the narrative:

   ```json
   {"frost": {"afi_100yr_F_days": 0, "afi_product_period": "...", "frost_depth_in": 0,
              "superseded_product_period": "...", "superseded_afi_100yr_F_days": 0},
    "pads": {"<PAD-ID>": {"governing_constraint": "...",
                          "foundation_decision": "SPREAD|IMPROVED_SPREAD",
                          "spread_only_cost_usd": 0, "improved_cost_usd": 0}},
    "campus": {"rigs_mobilised": 0, "mobilisation_cost_usd": 0, "total_cost_usd": 0,
               "pads_improved": ["..."]},
    "rejected_criteria": ["..."]}
   ```

   The narrative must state: the criteria that govern and the documents that were reviewed and set
   aside, with the reason; the bearing-capacity and settlement methods actually applied and the
   basis of the factor of safety used at each pad; the tolerable-movement criteria adopted and any
   competing criterion rejected; the ground-improvement design parameters with the authority for
   each; how every conflict between documents was resolved, with the governing value; and the
   reasoning behind the campus programme — which pads are improved, how many rigs are mobilised and
   why that number.

Keep the archive under 25 MB and 200 files.

## Grading

Pads are graded individually against the grader's own derivation from the same documents; a subset
of the pads is used for scoring. Requirement families are tagged HARD (bearing capacity and the
factor of safety, the groundwater correction, the bearing stratum, total and differential
settlement, minimum widths, frost protection, sliding, overturning and uplift of the shear-wall
footing, footing shear and reinforcement, the sulfate exposure condition and the concrete durability
limits, the aggregate-pier replacement ratio, stress ratio, stiffness modulus and treatment depth,
the mobilisation programme, and the prohibition on presumptive bearing values) or SOFT (schedule
completeness, parameter-file conformance, the verification-testing programme, and the design-basis
statements — four of which are judged by an LLM against verbatim quotes from `design_basis.md`).

### How your reported analysis values are reviewed

The grader re-derives the physics from **your own geometry** and checks that your design is safe.
Where it also compares a number you *reported*, the comparison is **one-sided and tolerant of
conservatism** — being more cautious than the grader's recomputation never costs you a family:

* a **capacity** you report may not be more permissive than the grader's recomputation by more than
  **6 %** (net allowable bearing pressure; sliding and uplift factors of safety, 20 %). Any bearing
  method at least as conservative as the general bearing-capacity equation of the governing
  foundations manual is accepted — including the least of three methods. There is **no lower bound**
  on a reported capacity;
* a **demand** you report may not fall below the grader's recomputation by more than **15 %**
  (applied net bearing pressure), **20 %** (settlement, eccentricity), **10 %** (top-of-pier
  stress). There is **no upper bound**;
* the recomputed **angular distortion between adjacent units** is graded against the criteria's own
  limit **exactly**. Both sides of that comparison are computed by the grader from your geometry
  with the settlement procedure the data room states, so no reporting band applies to it;
* required **flexural steel** is a lower bound with a **10 %** tolerance; the code minimum
  reinforcement ratios are exact;
* the recomputed **shear thickness** requirement is a lower bound evaluated with the most permissive
  strength-reduction factor in general use, so a footing designed by the shipped manual's own worked
  examples is thicker than required;
* the one-sided bands have a **sanity floor**: a reported net allowable bearing pressure may not
  fall below **half** the grader's recomputation (the least of three widely accepted methods is
  about 0.82 × of it, so the floor is more than three times clear of the most conservative method
  the criteria invite), and a reported settlement may not exceed the total-settlement limit you are
  designing to. Neither test costs a conservative solver anything;
* the **hard limits themselves are exact**: the total-settlement limit, the minimum footing widths,
  the minimum factors of safety, the exposure classes and the concrete limits, the
  replacement-ratio, top-of-pier-stress and treatment-depth bounds, and the owner's dimensioning
  grid and minimum footing thickness.

The governing constraint you name for a pad is accepted if it is a constraint that **selects** that
pad's design: either taking one 3-in step of plan width off any one foundation on the pad (with that
footing's shear thickness re-derived at the smaller width) would violate it, or your **own reported**
bearing, settlement or differential-settlement numbers put it at **80 %** or more of its limit
somewhere on the pad. Footing thickness and bearing elevation are dependent variables of this
problem - the thickness follows from shear and the elevation from frost - so `PUNCHING_SHEAR` is not
a pad-level governing constraint, and `FROST` is accepted only where the pad is founded at the frost
minimum and nothing else on it is near binding. All nine values remain legal per foundation in the
parameter file.

Per pad: a family earns credit only if it is **both** satisfied **and** registered. Let `p` be
the fraction of all 32 families satisfied-and-registered, multiplied by the register precision factor
described above, and `h` the fraction of the 22 HARD families satisfied-and-registered (not multiplied
by that factor). Let `O` be the programme credit = (a certified lower
bound on the cost of any compliant campus programme) / (the grader's repricing of **your** design
at the project unit prices), capped at 1.

The pad score is `0.4 p + 0.6 [h = 1] O'`, where `O' = clip((O - O_naive) / (1 - O_naive), 0, 1)` and
`O_naive` is the programme credit of a naive baseline programme. Thus a parseable pad earns programme
credit (none when the design cannot be repriced) only when all of its HARD families are
satisfied-and-registered (`h = 1`): an omitted citation or a physical
HARD violation forfeits the programme credit. A missing or
unparseable pad scores 0. The task score is the mean over the graded pads.

The lower bound comes from a relaxation of the campus problem, so the programme credit is strictly
below 1 for every attainable design; a cheaper compliant programme never scores worse than a more
expensive one, and the grader reprices your own decisions, so a programme that under-buys
mobilisations or misstates a quantity is repriced at what it actually costs. Reinforcement is priced
at the greater of the ratio you report and the ratio your design actually requires, so the tolerance
on the flexural steel cannot be spent on cost.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

title: Feasible data-center site design as an IFC model
summary: Generate an IFC site model for a two-phase data-center campus that satisfies all requirements in its approval document.
instruction:
# Design a phased data-center campus on a wetland-divided greenfield parcel as a 3D BIM model (`p6_002`)

## Situation

You are the site engineer for a two-hall data-center campus on a rectangular greenfield parcel. Two delineated wetlands divide the southern and northern developable areas, leaving one narrow upland corridor between them. The campus is delivered in two phases; each phase must stand alone as a working facility with complete power, access, and services. The authority having jurisdiction has issued a Development Standards and Conditions of Approval document. Every binding design requirement appears in that prose.

## Inputs

- `agent_view.json`: site geometry, two-phase building program, objective weights, network output schema, and the full `brief_document`. Coordinates use metres in a local CRS. Treat these instance data as authoritative.
- `docs/ifc_contract.md`: required IFC conventions.
- `docs/example.ifc`: a complete toy-site example demonstrating those conventions.
- `submission/model.ifc`: a valid IFC header and empty site to build upon.
- `oracle_client.py`: present in the workspace but unusable in this blind evaluation (see Verification).

## Goal

Place both data halls, the substation, generator yard, cooling plant, landscape berm, and stormwater retention area. Route the road and medium-voltage networks so that all 17 binding requirements are satisfied. A passing design is FEASIBLE. Among feasible designs, minimize `1.0 × MV-cable length + 0.3 × road length`; feasibility takes priority over optimization.

## Constraints

- The binding setbacks, separations, noise limits, stormwater sizing rules, phase requirements, and design-to-cost caps appear only in the prose brief. Some clauses refer to schedules elsewhere in the document, and some do not bind this site.
- Provide one continuous road network from one approved entrance on the designated frontage. Disconnected frontage stubs are not separate entrances and do not satisfy access.
- Buildings and roads must respect the wetland exclusions and buffers. Linear medium-voltage utilities may cross a wetland; roads and structures may not.
- The noise calculation treats each equipment footprint centroid as a point source at the greater of the building height and 2 m, uses a receiver height of 1.5 m, applies spherical spreading of `Lw − 20 log10(d) − 11 dB`, and energetically sums all sources. An intervening structure or berm that blocks the three-dimensional line of sight provides 10 dB insertion loss.
- Deliver an IFC4 BIM model as raw STEP text. The workspace contains no BIM library. Model each program building as an `IfcBuilding` with an extruded-solid footprint and the required identity property set. Embed the road, medium-voltage, and graph payload in the `DCD_Networks` property set on the `IfcSite`.

## Verification (blind evaluation)
This is a blind evaluation: no oracle is served in this run. `python3 oracle_client.py submission/model.ifc` cannot connect, and the verification protocol described in `Task.md` does not apply. The verifier and its libraries are not available in the workspace, and no score, verdict, or other feedback is returned before you submit. Plan the design and IFC serialization to correctness before submitting.
Scoring of the final `submission/model.ifc`: `1.0` for a FEASIBLE design; otherwise one half of the fraction of the 17 binding requirements satisfied; `0.0` when the model fails an IFC parse, extraction, semantic, schema, or geometry gate.

## Expected output

Submit `submission/model.ifc`. The final grade uses the final file only. Feasible models score `1.0`; infeasible extracted models receive the partial-credit score described above; hard-gate failures score `0.0`.

# Frame extension over an occupied floor — the method package

## The situation

You are the construction engineer for a three-lift reinforced concrete frame
extension built over a building whose ground floor stays in use throughout. The
design is fixed and is in the corpus: the storey elevations, the column grid and
sections, the slab thickness and the zone breakdown. **How it gets built is
not.** The construction sequence and the temporary works that make each stage of
it stand up and be reachable are yours, and they are what you issue.

Read `handover/instruction_to_engineer.md` first. It says what the package is
and what the corpus holds.

The rest is the project's own record set: the architect's IFC exports and the
design model schedules taken off them, the issued activity list with its
durations, crane hours and logic, the zone work schedule with the quantities,
the site plan data — the crane chart, the standing positions, the overhead
services, the parts of the building still occupied — the shoring and scaffold
catalogues with their capacities and costs, and the rules: the site's temporary
works procedure TWP-09 with its parameter schedule, and the five public criteria
it adopts.

The limits you have to work to — how much load a shore post may carry, how wide
a platform must be, when a scaffold has to be tied and where, how high a
guardrail sits, when forms may be struck and what that costs you in reshoring,
how many crane hours there are in a shift, what the yard holds, how many gangs
there are, and when the job has to be finished — **are all written down in that
corpus and none of them are restated here.** Finding the governing clause,
reading it and working to it is part of the job, and it is measured (see *The
constraint register*).

## What to deliver

Write these six files into the output directory (`output/`), not into the input
tree. CSV headers are matched case- and punctuation-insensitively; the columns
below are required, and extra columns you find useful are ignored rather than
penalised.

| File | Required columns |
|---|---|
| `construction_sequence.csv` | `activity_id`, `zone`, `level`, `activity_type`, `predecessors`, `duration_days`, `start_day`, `finish_day`, `crew`, `crane_hours`, `workspace_volume_cf` |
| `stability_check.csv` | `stage_id`, `zone`, `level`, `lateral_system`, `demand_lb`, `capacity_lb`, `verdict` |
| `occupancy_report.csv` | `zone_lift`, `zone`, `level`, `occupied_from_day`, `occupied_to_day`, `shored_from_day`, `shored_to_day`, `crane_hours_total`, `laydown_units` |
| `temporary_works.json` | see below |
| `constraint_register.csv` | `requirement`, `document`, `clause`, `value`, `unit`, `items_bound` |
| `method_note.md` | prose, at least **200 words** |

Cover **every zone-lift in the zone work schedule**, and carry **every activity
in the issued activity list** — one row each, keeping the issued `activity_id`.
`duration_days` must be the issued duration and `finish_day` must equal
`start_day + duration_days`; days are whole numbers counted from day 0.

**Work you leave out of the programme is still charged against the site-wide
limits.** There is one crane, one yard, one laydown and one completion date, and
they are drawn on by every zone-lift on the site. An activity that is not in
`construction_sequence.csv` has no day for the verifier to place it on, so it is
charged at the **busiest day you do declare**: its crane hours over its issued
duration, and — for any zone-lift whose activities are not all programmed — its
shored area, its scaffold face, its laydown units and a gang, with the programme
unable to finish before the earliest day the issued logic allows that work to
finish. A zone-lift with no dates is also treated as occupying its zone. Omitting
work does not buy yard stock or crane hours; it costs them.

`stability_check.csv` carries **one row per zone-lift** and is keyed by its
`level` and `zone` columns. `lateral_system` is `temporary_bracing` or
`adjacent_diaphragm`, compared case- and punctuation-insensitively, and
`verdict` is `pass` where the check is satisfied. Any other value is not
recognised.

`occupancy_report.csv` carries **one row per zone-lift**. Its days and totals
are checked against the programme you yourself declared, so a report that does
not agree with your own sequence is a false statement about the site.

`workspace_volume_cf` is the volume the activity occupies: for a scaffold
erection or strike, the zone's face length times the scaffold's base width times
its height above grade; for everything else, the zone's plan area times the
clear height of the lift.

### The tolerances the verifier applies

Several checks compare a number you declare against the same number recomputed
from the corpus. Every tolerance the verifier uses is listed here, because a
threshold you cannot see is one you cannot aim at.

| what is compared | tolerance |
|---|---|
| `shoring.design_load_per_post_lb` against the zone's design load times the square of your grid | 2 percent |
| `stability_check.csv` `demand_lb` against the recomputed lateral demand | 5 percent |
| `scaffold.maximum_intended_load_lb` against the duty class's load | exact |
| `workspace_volume_cf` against the geometry | 5 percent |
| `occupancy_report.csv` `crane_hours_total` against the sum of the issued crane hours | 0.02 hours |
| `occupancy_report.csv` day columns and `laydown_units` | exact |
| `scaffold.platform_capacity_lb`, `crane.rated_capacity_lb` | exact / 2 percent respectively |
| `crane.radius_ft` against the distance from the standing position to the zone centroid | 2 ft |
| `scaffold.height_ft` against the level's height above grade | 0.51 ft |
| `scaffold.height_to_base_ratio` | 0.05 |
| each entry of `scaffold.tie_levels_ft` against the horizontal member the clause puts it at | half a frame lift |
| `duration_days` against the issued duration, and `finish_day − start_day` | exact |

Anything not in this table is a threshold you will find in a shipped document,
not one this note withholds.

### `temporary_works.json`

A single JSON object with `designer`, `drawing_reference` and `zone_lifts`.
`zone_lifts` maps each zone-lift id to an object with `shoring`, `reshore`,
`scaffold`, `bracing` and `crane`. Keys are matched case- and
punctuation-insensitively. The fields the verifier reads:

* `shoring`: `post_type`, `spacing_ft`, `posts`, `design_load_per_post_lb`
* `reshore`: `required` (`yes` / `no`), `posts`, `install_day`, `remove_day`
* `scaffold`: `system`, `base_width_ft`, `bays`, `frame_lifts`, `frames`,
  `planks_per_bay`, `platform_width_in`, `platform_capacity_lb`,
  `platform_levels`, `planks`,
  `guardrail_height_in`, `guardrails`, `height_ft`, `height_to_base_ratio`,
  `tie_levels_ft` (a list of elevations in feet), `tie_columns`, `ties`,
  `maximum_intended_load_lb`, `front_edge_gap_in`, `front_edge_guardrail`,
  `mudsill`, `bearing_pressure_psf`, `access_means`, `fall_protection`
* `bracing`: `lateral_system`, `braced_bays`, `capacity_lb`. `braced_bays`
  must be a whole number greater than or equal to zero for every lateral system;
  use `0` when `lateral_system` is `adjacent_diaphragm`.
* `crane`: `position`, `radius_ft`, `rated_capacity_lb`,
  `encroachment_option` (`option1` / `option2` / `option3`), `min_approach_ft`,
  `demarcated_radius_ft`

`access_means` is one of `stair_tower`, `hook_on_ladder`, `attachable_ladder`,
`stairway_type_ladder`, `portable_ladder`, `integral_access_frame`.
`fall_protection` is one of `guardrail`, `personal_fall_arrest`, `both`.
Anything else is not recognised.

## How your package is checked

Your programme is **re-simulated**, not compared with a key. Your own start and
finish days are replayed against a pristine copy of the site model and every
demand is recomputed from the rows you wrote: each issued dependency, the
strength-gain age your own striking method demands, the crane hours drawn on
each day, the soffit area and scaffold face standing in the yard on each day,
the gangs at work, the laydown, the zones occupied and the stair cores shored.
A programme in a different order is not wrong. A programme whose occupancy
report or whose declared loads do not agree with the programme it declares is.

The temporary-works design is checked the same way: every capacity, width,
ratio, tie interval, clearance and bearing pressure is recomputed from the
shipped catalogues and the shipped clauses against the numbers you declared. A
heavier design than the cheapest one is not wrong; it costs more.

## The constraint register

`constraint_register.csv` is where you record the requirements you actually
applied: one row per requirement, naming the document and the clause it comes
from, its value and unit where it has one, and what it binds. It is scored, and
two floors are stated here because a threshold you cannot see is one you cannot
aim at:

- **register recall floor 0.55** — at least 0.55 of the requirements the grader
  indexes must be present in your register;
- **value-agreement floor 0.40** — at least 0.40 of them must additionally carry
  the right value.

Filing *more* genuine requirements than the grader happens to index is neutral:
thoroughness is not punished. What counts against you is a row that should not
have been filed at all — a citation to a document that is not in force, to a
scope that is not in this package, or to a clause that does not exist.

A requirement the grader holds to be **hard** and which is missing from your
register fails the register family of every zone-lift it binds, which is one of
that zone-lift's hard families (see *What is scored*).

## The method note

`method_note.md` is prose and it is read for four things: which document
governs where the issued set disagrees with itself, the striking and reshoring
method you adopted, the constraint that governs each zone, and the margins you
applied. At least 200 words.

## What is scored

Your score is the mean over the **held-out zone-lifts**, which you cannot query.
Each is checked against thirty constraint families, fifteen of them hard: fourteen
engineering families and the register family, which a zone-lift passes only if
every hard requirement that binds it is registered. A zone-lift scores

most 1. A hard miss removes O. Four of the hard families are **shared across the whole

# Pacific Crest Space Force Annex — conveyance study for the 13.8 kV site distribution

You are the electrical engineer and cost estimator of the design-build contractor for solicitation FA4610-26-R-0031 at
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. The Government requires a **conveyance study**
before the 35 % design: for seven medium-voltage circuits — from the site substation SS-1 to the medium-voltage
switchgear lineups of the Mission Support Facility MB-1, to the Central Utility Plant CUP-1, to the gate house and to
the lift station, from CUP-1 to warehouse W-3, and inside MB-1 from switchgear MSG-A to unit substation USS-A1 — decide
which conveyance is the most cost-effective one that the governing criteria permit, design it, and price every
conveyance type the study must evaluate.

The contract documents are in this workspace: the RFP section with the study requirements, labor classification
plan and estimating basis; the installation electrical design standard; the governing DoD criteria and guide
specifications; federal regulations; the site utility plan, one-line diagram, building plans, utility survey and tree survey; the
geotechnical report and boring logs; the protective device settings schedule; cable data, the approved cable
submittal and ampacity tables; the labor-unit database, crew book and payroll burden; supplier, rental and
subcontract quotes; wage determinations; equipment rate schedules; escalation and producer price indexes; and the
Government estimate template. Some folders hold superseded material; the transmittal says what is current and the
installation standard sets the order of precedence. Government-furnished documents are not guaranteed free of
errors — the RFP requires the study to report the ones you find. The NFPA 70, IEEE C2 and NECA texts are not
provided; the project is governed by the documents provided.

## What to deliver

A study package for all seven circuits (items `C01` … `C07`, defined in RFP Section 01 11 00):

1. **For every item, every conveyance type the study must evaluate** (RFP 1.4): whether the governing criteria permit
   it for this circuit and the clause that decides, its take-off, labor hours, the labor, equipment and material
   rates used, its direct cost, the estimate roll-up to total project cost, and its cost per linear foot.
2. **For every item, the recommended conveyance designed** so that it can be built as priced: the route on the site
   (or building) plan, each segment's installation method, burial depth, duct arrangement and spares, reinforcement,
   trench protective system and dewatering; manholes, poles and pull boxes with their positions; the cable size and
   number of parallel sets from the ampacity at the governing installation condition; the cable pulling calculation
   of every pull.
3. **A study report** (`conveyance_study_report.md`, `.pdf` or `.docx`) presenting, per item, the recommendation and
   the tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear foot of each conveyance type evaluated.

Among designs the criteria permit, the one with the lower total project cost, estimated by the RFP estimating basis,
is the better design.

## Coordinates

## Deliverable format

Write `output/submission.zip` containing `conveyance_study.xlsx` and the report at the zip root. Use the sheet names
and header row of `templates/conveyance_study_TEMPLATE.xlsx` (header in row 1, one record per row; extra columns are
ignored). Types, methods and codes are those of the RFP and the cost documents: conveyance types `CEDB`, `UEDB`,
`DBC`, `HDD`, `OH` (site items) and `RMC`, `EMT`, `TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD` (item C05); segment methods `CE`
(concrete-encased ductbank), `UE` (conduit without encasement), `DB` (direct-buried cable), `HDD`, `JB`
(jack-and-bore rigid steel conduit), `JS` (jack-and-sleeve), `OH` (overhead span), and for C05 `RMC`, `EMT`,
`TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD`; take-off codes are the labor-unit database codes, the supplier quote item codes, and `SUB-HDD`,
`SUB-JB`, `SUB-JS` for the subcontract quotes (dollars in `subcontract_usd`).

**Items** — one row per item: `item_id`, `recommended_type`, `cable_size` (AWG/kcmil as in the cable data, blank if
none), `sets`, `overhead_conductor` (ACSR size, blank if none), `design_current_a`, `ampacity_per_set_a` (at the
governing condition), `route_length_ft`, `total_project_cost_usd`, `cost_per_lf_usd`.

**Segments** — the recommended route of each item, one row per segment in order from the source end:
`item_id`, `seg_no`, `method`, `route` (polyline `x1,y1; x2,y2; …`; consecutive segments share end points),
`cover_in` (finished grade to the top of the duct envelope, conduit or cable; blank for OH and C05), `duct_rows`,
`duct_cols`, `duct_size_in`, `spare_ducts`, `shared_with` (other items whose circuits occupy the same ductbank on this
segment, comma-separated), `reinforced` (`Y`/`N`), `soil_type` (OSHA `A`/`B`/`C`), `protective_system` (`none`,
`slope` or `box`), `slope_h_per_v`, `dewatering` (`Y`/`N`).

**Structures** — manholes, poles and pull boxes of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `structure_id`, `kind`
(`MH`, `POLE`, `RISER_POLE`, `PULLBOX`), `x_ft`, `y_ft` (on the route), `pole_height_ft`, `guys`, `dead_end` (`Y`/`N`),
`protective_system`, `slope_h_per_v` (manhole excavations).

**Pulls** — every cable pull of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `pull_id`, `from_id`, `to_id` (structure ids, or
`START` / `END` for the item's terminals), `length_ft`, `max_tension_lb`, `max_sidewall_lb_per_ft`, `jam_ratio`,
`fill_pct`. A vertex of an underground route that is not a structure is a field long-sweep bend.

**Alternatives** — one row per item and conveyance type evaluated: `item_id`, `type`, `admissible` (`Y`/`N`),
`governing_clause` (document and clause that permits or excludes it), `length_ft`, `labor_mh`, `labor_usd`,
`equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`, `direct_cost_usd`, `jooh_usd`, `hooh_usd`, `profit_usd`,
`bond_usd`, `escalation_usd`, `contract_cost_usd`, `contingency_usd`, `sioh_usd`, `total_project_cost_usd`,
`cost_per_lf_usd`, `recommended` (`Y` on exactly one row per item).

**Takeoff** — the priced lines behind every alternative: `item_id`, `type`, `code`, `quantity`, `unit`, `labor_mh`,
`labor_usd`, `equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`.

**LaborRates** — `class` (crew book position), `wd_group`, `classification`, `base_usd`, `fringe_usd`, `burden_pct`,
`loaded_rate_usd`. **EquipmentRates** — `equipment_id`, `description`, `source`, `hourly_rate_usd`.

**Markups** — `parameter`, `value` for `jooh_pct`, `hooh_pct`, `profit_pct`, `bond_rate_pct`, `escalation_factor`,
`contingency_pct`, `sioh_pct`, `area_cost_factor_applied` (the factor applied to the estimate, `1` if none) and
`wage_determination` (number and modification used).

**Register** — the requirements you applied: `req_id`, `document` (number/title, with revision where documents have
several), `clause` (section, paragraph, table or figure), `requirement`, `value`, `applies_to`.

**Findings** — every error or inconsistency found in the Government-furnished documents: `finding_id`, `document`,
`location`, `defect` (with the conflicting values), `correction` (what you used).

### Live formulas

In **Alternatives**, `direct_cost_usd` through `cost_per_lf_usd` must be formulas referencing the cells they are
computed from (and the **Markups** values), and in **LaborRates** `loaded_rate_usd` must be a formula; the reviewer
recalculates the workbook and changes inputs to confirm the results follow. Use ordinary arithmetic and common
functions (`SUM`, `SUMIFS`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `ROUND`, `IF`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `VLOOKUP`) with plain cell references. No
spreadsheet application is installed in this workspace; Python with `openpyxl` is, and a workbook written by it without

# Device takeoff and priced bill of materials for a data hall -- ec_0205_d100

You are the electrical estimator for a data hall. The project folder contains
the architectural and MEP drawing set, the electrical symbol legend, the
device plans, the enlarged plans, the device and mounting schedule, any
addenda, the electrical and fire-alarm specifications, the manufacturer's
device catalogue, a price list, the owner's procurement requirements and the
takeoff criteria manual.

**The device plans carry no labels.** Every device is a symbol, and the symbol
legend is the only thing that says what each symbol means. **No document in
the folder states the quantity of anything.** Assemble them.

Not every device is drawn. A keyed note that requires a device is part of the
drawing, and the number of devices it requires is a census of geometry on
another sheet. An area cross-referenced to an enlarged plan is drawn empty on
its parent plan. Where an addendum postdates a sheet's revision, the addendum
governs for what it describes.

A symbol in the legend with no instance on any plan has a quantity of zero. A
symbol on a plan that is **not in the legend is not a scheduled device**:
carry no quantity for it and list it as an unresolved item in your basis, with
its sheet and its location. Guessing what it might be is worse than saying you
could not resolve it.

A device is not only a device. Each one needs an assembly of catalogue items,
a box and whatever ring, cover or accessory its condition calls for, and
which of those is permitted depends on where the device is --
the wall's construction and fire rating, whether the area is damp, whether the
device is on the emergency branch, and how it is mounted. The specification
says what each condition requires; the catalogue says what each item is;
nothing joins the two for you.

The criteria manual says how a condition is determined but leaves four cases
unstated, and these conventions govern them. A condition E-002 sets
(EMERGENCY by branch, IG, CEILING or ACCESS-FLOOR by mounting) takes precedence
over every other, and a duct smoke detector is carried under CEILING wherever
it is. Otherwise, a device inside an area hatched DAMP on A-102 is DAMP. Any
other device that takes a wall condition takes the construction of the wall on
A-102 nearest to it, measured to the wall's centreline, whether or not it
stands against that wall. A device required by a keyed note and drawn nowhere
takes the construction of the wall the note names (for a device at a door, the
wall that door is in on A-102), or DRY-STUD where the note names none. The catalogue carries no while-in-use hood: where the
specification requires one, state it in the basis and carry no line for it.

Hand back `output/submission.zip` containing

- `takeoff.csv` -- one row per device type: `type_mark, description, quantity`
- `locations.csv` -- `sheet, type_mark, grid_bay, condition, count`; one row
  per grid bay per type per sheet, NOT one row per device
- `bom.csv` -- the priced bill: `line_item, description, for_type_mark,
  condition, quantity, unit, unit_price, extended_price`, including every
  assembly item each device drags in. **Two kinds of row**, and the
  `for_type_mark` column says which: an ATTRIBUTION row names a type mark and
  a condition and carries the quantity THAT PAIR REQUIRES (its device count
  times the item's multiplicity in the assembly you chose); a PURCHASE row
  carries `(PURCHASE)` and `(STOCK)`, one per catalogue item, and carries the
  quantity you BUY. The criteria manual states the schema in full
- `register.csv` -- every requirement in the takeoff criteria manual, the
  document and clause you satisfied it against, the value you used, and how
- `basis.md` -- the counting convention applied with its clause, the sheets
  each type was counted from, which issue governed and why, every unresolved
  symbol, the condition split and where it came from, the assembly chosen for
  each condition and the clause that permits it, the spare-stock and carton
  method, and the basket total

**Counts are exact. There is no tolerance on a quantity.** Every device type
with an instance in the set must be present, every quantity must be right, and
nothing may be invented.

The bill is priced on the quantity the WORK REQUIRES, at the price list rate
for the band that quantity earns. Cartons and the owner's spare stock are
constraints on what you BUY, not terms in what the work costs: buying too
little fails outright, and buying in part cartons or without the owner's
spare fails too. The criteria manual is the contract; where a source it cites
is not in the folder, the manual's restatement governs.

| `StepLoad` | `step`, `loads`, `step_kva_start`, `voltage_dip_pct`, `recovery_s`: one row per load step, in the order the loads are placed on the engine-generator |
| `Register` | `req_id`, `document` (number/title, with revision or change where there are several), `clause` (paragraph, table, note or row), `requirement`, `value` (the governing number or choice), `applies_to` (section numbers) |
| `Findings` | `finding_id`, `document`, `location`, `defect`, `correction`: errors or inconsistencies you found in the furnished documents and how you resolved them |

## Section format

Each section document must read, as plain paragraphs of text:

- `SECTION nn nn nn` (the section number), the section title, and the section date line;
- `PART 1   GENERAL`, `PART 2   PRODUCTS`, `PART 3   EXECUTION` (a part without content reads `Not used.`);
- articles numbered as typed text, `1.1 REFERENCES`, `1.2 ...`, with upper-case titles; lower-level paragraphs
  `1.2.1 Title`; list items `a.`, `(1)`, `(a)`, `1.`;
- `-- End of Section --` as the last paragraph.

Numbering, list markers and section headings must be literal text in the paragraphs; automatic Word list numbering is
not read. Only paragraph text is read (tables in a section are read cell by cell as paragraphs). Any tool that writes a
valid `.docx` (WordprocessingML package) is fine; no word processor is installed in this workspace, and a `.docx` can be
written with the Python standard library (`zipfile` plus the three required parts: `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`,

files are text formats and can be parsed with the standard library.

## How the package is judged

Each delivered section is judged as one item against requirements recomputed from the project documents,
independently of wording; values are compared after unit conversion. The design-basis sheets are judged by re-running
the calculations against the design you declare, and the numbers you report are checked against that re-run. A section
with an unresolved choice, or whose design is unsafe or unbuildable, fails a hard requirement family.
Specifications are performance-based and must not be more restrictive than the governing requirement
(FAR 11.002(a)(1)(ii)); a design that meets every limit without over-providing earns the most objective credit. A hard
governing requirement that a section's design rests on and that is missing from your `Register` fails one more hard
family of that section. Each section scores `0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O`, where `p` is the weighted fraction of the section's
requirement families passed, `h` the weighted fraction of its hard families passed (`[h = 1]` is 1 when every hard
family passes, else 0), and `O` its over-specification credit: a failed hard family zeroes the `O` term.

# Building A2 — roof diaphragm shears and shear wall loads for wind

You are the delegated engineer for the **lateral package** of Building A2 at the Northern Divide
Data Campus, in Lewis and Clark County, Montana: a single-storey data hall with a steel roof deck
on joists and girders, carried laterally by precast concrete wall panels acting as shear walls on
every exterior building line, with a parapet cantilevering above the roof deck.

Your job is to work out **how the wind gets from the wall panels into the roof deck diaphragm and
back out into the shear walls**, to design the deck, the chords and collectors and the panel
connections that carry it, and to hand over the package the Engineer of Record will check: plan
drawings of the diaphragm unit shears and the shear wall loads, the schedules behind them, and a
calculation package.

The building is not the clean rectangle the 2024 drawings show. The as-built geometry is in the
2026 federated model and the roof line scan.

## What you are given

The task folder (project/, library/ and templates/) is the document set issued for this package: the structural design criteria, the
boundary-layer wind study and its coefficient data, the topographic study, the AHJ letter, the
survey and the roof line scan, the 2026 federated model, the architectural and structural
drawings, the precast panel drawings and schedule, the deck, chord and connection catalogues, the
owner's basis of design, the submittal specification, and the public standards library. It also
holds superseded revisions and a study of a different building on the same campus; part of the
job is knowing which document governs.

Nothing has been pre-digested for you. Every parameter you need is in those files — including the
analysis procedure the criteria requires you to use, and the verification example it publishes so
you can check your implementation before you trust it.

## What you must deliver

workbooks and the drawing are in `templates/`):

**1. `lateral_schedule.xlsx`** — nine worksheets.

* `DeckZones`: one row per deck zone —
  `zone_id, deck_code, G_prime_used_kip_per_in, capacity_asd_plf, area_sf, cost_usd`.
  `G_prime_used_kip_per_in` is the shear stiffness you actually used for that zone and
  `capacity_asd_plf` the shear capacity you checked against.
* `ChordSchedule`: one row per chord and collector line — `chord_id, section_code, length_ft,
  cost_usd`.
* `Piers`: one row per pier — `pier_id, panel, line, s0_ft, s1_ft, width_ft, thickness_in,
  top_z_ft, k_kip_per_in, embeds, tiedown`. `s0_ft`/`s1_ft` are the pier's extent along its wall
  line, `top_z_ft` the top of that panel, `k_kip_per_in` the stiffness you assigned it, `embeds`
  the number of deck-to-panel embeds on that panel and `tiedown` `yes` or `no`.
* `ShearWalls`: one row per wind scenario per wall line — `scenario, line, line_load_plf,
  reaction_kips`. `line_load_plf` is the roof-level line load on that wall line and
  `reaction_kips` the load that wall line takes out of the diaphragm. Report unit shears, line
  loads, reactions, chord forces and deflections as **magnitudes**; the scenario already says
  which way the wind blows, and either sign convention is read the same way.
* `Diaphragm`: one row per wind scenario, wall line and report station — `scenario, line,
  station_frac, unit_shear_plf`. The criteria fixes which stations are reported; use those.
* `Chords`: one row per wind scenario per chord and collector line — `scenario, chord_id,
  force_kips`.
* `Drift`: one row per wind scenario per global axis — `scenario, direction, deflection_in`.
* `Convergence`: one row per mesh refinement level — `level, mesh_size_ft, elements,
  max_unit_shear_plf, key_reaction_kips`, with `key_reaction_kips` the reaction of wall line W in
  scenario W01.
* `Cost`: `item, quantity, unit_cost_usd, total_usd`, one row per cost item, summing to the
  installed cost of the package.

**2. `diaphragm_plan.dxf`** — the plan view drawings, on the building grid in feet, with the
layers and the content the submittal specification requires.

**3. `constraint_register.xlsx`** — sheet `Register`, columns
`document, clause, requirement, value, units, items`: the requirements you applied, where each
one comes from, the value it sets, and the items it binds.

**4. `calculations.pdf`** — the calculation package, in the format and with the sections the
criteria and the submittal specification require.

**5. `design_basis.md`** — the design basis narrative, carrying the two tables the submittal
specification defines and, in prose, every conflict between issued documents that you resolved
and how.

## How it is graded

Per wind scenario: the package must be present and parseable; every constraint family is checked;
and the objective credit is the ratio of a certified cost bound to your installed cost, paid only
when you miss no hard family.

    score = 0.4 * p + 0.6 * [h = 1] * O

where `p` is the fraction of the 36 constraint families you both satisfied **and** registered, `h`
is the fraction of the 22 hard families you both satisfied and registered (`[h = 1]` is 1 when all
22 are, else 0), and `O` is the objective credit (at most 1). A hard miss zeroes the `O` term. The

# DC-2 Helena data centre — roof deck design for gravity and lateral loads

You are the structural engineer for Building A of the DC-2 data centre in Lewis and Clark County, Montana.
The roof framing is fixed and is not yours to change: open-web steel joists at 6 ft-0 in on centre spanning
30 ft between joist girders, over a 240 ft by 180 ft footprint, with the deck spanning across the joists in
three-span continuous conditions. Your job is the **roof deck**: its gage, its support-fastener pattern, its
sidelap connectors, and where each of those changes across the roof.

The project documents are in `project/`; the published standards the project cites are in `library/`; blank
deliverable templates are in `templates/`. The roof carries a rooftop equipment enclosure, equipment
screens, rooftop units, parapets and framed openings — the three-dimensional record of all of it is the
structural model in `project/15_model/`, and the two-dimensional drawings do not all agree with it or with
each other. Work out which documents govern and what they require.

The deck must carry the gravity loads, including the snow drifts the roof's own obstructions create; it must
carry the in-plane diaphragm shears from wind and seismic to the braced frames; its attachment must hold the
roof down under wind uplift; and among designs that do all of that, the lowest **installed cost** at the cost
plan rates is preferred.

The deck's shear stiffness is a result of your design, and the distribution of the roof force between the
eight braced frames depends on it — a stiffer deck does not simply have more capacity in reserve.

## Deliverable

Write one file, `output/submission.zip`, containing at its root:

### 1. `deck_design.xlsx` — the design (sheet names and column headers exactly as below)

All plan coordinates are **project grid coordinates in feet**: x along grids 1→9, y along grids A→G, origin
at grid 1-A.

* **Zones**: `zone_id`, `x0_ft`, `y0_ft`, `x1_ft`, `y1_ft`, `gage`, `support_pattern`, `sidelap_type`,
  `sidelap_per_span`. One row per **rectangle**. A zone may be made of several rectangles — repeat the
  `zone_id`, and every rectangle of a zone must carry the same gage, pattern, sidelap type and count. The
  rectangles must not overlap and together must cover every part of the roof that receives deck.
  `support_pattern` is written `36/n` for n fasteners across the 36 in cover width at each support.
* **DesignBasis**: `key`, `value` — one row per key, all of:
  `PG_PSF`, `CE`, `CT`, `IS`, `PF_PSF`, `GAMMA_PCF`, `LR_PSF`, `QH_PSF`, `A_ZONE_FT`, `SDS`, `IE`, `R`,
  `W_SEISMIC_PSF`, `FPX_KIP`, `WIND_X_KIP`, `WIND_Y_KIP`, `DIAPHRAGM_CLASS`.
  `W_SEISMIC_PSF` is the effective seismic weight per square foot of roof, `FPX_KIP` the roof diaphragm
  design force, `WIND_X_KIP` and `WIND_Y_KIP` the roof-level wind forces, `DIAPHRAGM_CLASS` the
  classification the design criteria ask for.
* **Drifts**: `location`, `face`, `peak_surcharge_psf`, `band_from_ft`, `band_to_ft` — one row for each
  of `MEP-PH-1` face `W`, `SCR-N` face `S`, `PARAPET` face `N`, `RTU-1` face `E`. `peak_surcharge_psf` is
  the drift surcharge at the face, over and above the balanced snow load; `band_from_ft` and `band_to_ft`
  are the plan coordinates bounding the drift, on the axis normal to that face — x for an east or west
  face, y for a north or south face — running from the face outwards. For `PARAPET` face `N`, the face is
  the inside of the north parapet.
* **CalcSummary**: `zone_id`, `governing_scenario`, `shear_demand_plf`, `shear_capacity_plf`,
  `gravity_demand_psf`, `gravity_capacity_psf`, `uplift_demand_psf`, `uplift_capacity_psf` — one row per
  zone, each demand being the largest anywhere in that zone over all scenarios, and `governing_scenario`
  the scenario id (`S01`…`S10`) whose demand/capacity ratio is the largest for that zone.
* **Diaphragm**: `scenario`, `direction`, `max_shear_plf`, `max_deflection_in`, `chord_force_kip`,
  `collector_force_kip`, `classification` — one row per lateral scenario.
* **BOM**: `item`, `quantity`, `unit` — at least `deck area <g> gage` in sf for every gage used,
  `support fasteners` and `sidelap connectors` in ea.

### 2. `roof_deck_plan.dxf` — the roof framing plan

In **feet**, in the same grid coordinates. One closed `LWPOLYLINE` per zone rectangle on layer
`S-DECK-ZONE`, and for each zone a `TEXT` label containing its `zone_id`, placed inside one of that zone's
rectangles, on layer `S-DECK-TEXT`. Show the framing on layer `S-FRAMING` and the roof openings on layer
`S-OPENING`.

### 3. `constraint_register.xlsx` — the requirements you designed to

Sheet `Register` with columns `document`, `clause`, `value`, `applies_to`: one row per requirement you
applied, naming the governing document (its title or document number), the clause, section or table, the
numerical value with units where there is one, and what it binds. Only the first 150 rows are read. A row
that cites a superseded or non-governing document, or whose value contradicts the clause it cites (it gives
a different number for a quantity that clause states), counts against the register; every number in a row
must be a value the cited clause states (or an equivalent of it), so one wrong number makes the row count
against the register even when another is right; rows without numbers do not count against it; a row that
cites requirements of more than one document or more than three clauses, or carries more than 8 numbers, is
not credited and counts against the register. If more than 40 % of the rows read count against the register,
none of it is credited. A requirement you satisfy but do not register earns less credit than one you satisfy
and register; a governing requirement missing from the register forfeits the credit of every family it governs.

### 4. `design_basis.md`

A narrative: which documents governed where they conflict and why, the snow and seismic bases, how the
diaphragm was analysed and classified, the zoning decisions and what drove each one.

## How the deliverable is judged

The design is re-analysed independently in every design scenario, with the loads, capacities and stiffnesses
derived from the project documents. Each scenario is credited for the constraints the design satisfies and
documents — hard constraints (gravity strength, deflection and bearing, diaphragm shear, in-plane
deflection, chord and collector forces, uplift, attachment rules, zoning rules, procurement, and the design
basis values) and softer documentation and consistency checks (schedule completeness, the drawing, the bill
of materials, the governing-scenario declaration). Cost credit is measured against a certified lower bound
on the installed cost of any compliant design: each scenario scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p is the
fraction of the 28 constraint families credited, h the fraction of the 21 hard families credited ([h = 1] is
1 when all 21 are, else 0), and O the bound divided by your installed cost, at most 1. A hard miss withholds
the cost credit.

**The design scenarios.** `S01` gravity with the roof live load; `S02` gravity with balanced snow and the
drifts at the equipment enclosure; `S03` gravity with balanced snow and the parapet drifts; `S04` gravity
with balanced snow and the drifts at the rooftop units and the equipment screen; `S05` wind along x;
`S06` wind along y; `S07` seismic along x; `S08` seismic along y; `S09` components-and-cladding uplift;
`S10` seismic along x with the collectors amplified by the overstrength factor.

**Checking conventions.** The roof is checked on a grid of cells one joist spacing by one sidelap module
(6 ft by 6 ft), and a cell must carry the worst demand occurring anywhere inside it; zone rectangle
boundaries fall on those same lines. A cell any part of which falls inside a framed roof opening carries no
deck, so a framed opening takes out every cell it touches, not only the cells it fills. The in-plane analysis the grader re-runs is the one the design criteria
and the lateral analysis report describe: shear panels one joist bay wide by one girder bay deep carrying
pure shear with the deck's G', axial bars along every joist line and every girder line with the axial
stiffnesses the lateral report gives, the perimeter edge member added to the boundary lines, and each braced
frame as a spring of half its stiffness at each of its two column lines; within a panel the shear flow is
constant, so deck strips stacked across its depth act in series. A small spring on every free degree of
freedom regularises the solution, and a scenario in which more than 2 % of the applied force is carried by
those springs rather than by the deck, the framing and the braced frames has no load path and fails. Wind enters along the two wall lines
perpendicular to the force, half at each; the seismic inertial force is spread over the plan by tributary
area; the stated eccentricity is applied as a plan couple. The reported chord force is the largest axial
force in the chord lines for that direction, and the reported collector force the largest axial force in a
perimeter member within one bay of a braced frame of that direction, amplified where the scenario says so.
Values you report are compared with the re-analysis within the tolerances an engineer would expect of an
independent model, not to the last digit.
